methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective single-center cohort design is appropriate for external validation of a prognostic score, and the use of competing-risks analysis (death without recurrence as competing event, Section 2.6 and 3.3) is a methodological strength. However, no power calculation is reported, the exclusion criteria sentence in Section 2.1 is truncated ('Patients were excluded from this study in case of') leaving selection criteria unspecified, and the validation lacks standard discrimination (C-index/AUC) and calibration metrics expected for a prognostic model validation. Multivariable Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier methods are appropriate, HRs with CIs are reported, but there is no handling-of-missing-data description, no sensitivity analysis stratified by transplant era (acknowledged as a limitation), and the post-hoc RETREAT+ modification is exploratory with no multiplicity correction.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a single individual retrospective cohort study (298 consecutive LT recipients at a Northern Italian center, 2000–2022), which maps to Oxford LoE 2b. Endpoints (HCC recurrence, overall survival) are patient-relevant and the question — risk stratification after LT for HCC — is clinically important given expanding eligibility criteria. Translational relevance is moderate: the score is already validated and in use, so the work supports continued application in a European real-world setting and could inform surveillance intensity and immunosuppression decisions, but it does not change practice or offer a new tool.

reporting_quality.justification: For a prognostic model external validation, TRIPOD applies; several key items are missing or incomplete, including explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria (truncated sentence in Section 2.1), handling of missing data, model performance discrimination (C-statistic/AUC) and calibration (calibration plots or observed-vs-expected tables), and a flow diagram of patient inclusion. Baseline table and HRs are present (Tables 1–4), but TRIPOD items on predictors measurement blinding, calibration, and model updating are not addressed. No data-availability statement, repository, or analytic code reference is visible in the blinded text, so reproducibility posture is minimal.

novelty_literature.justification: This is an incremental external validation of an already well-validated score (Mehta 2017; multiple European/UK/UNOS validations cited as refs 18–21). The novelty claims — Italian setting, longer 2000–2022 timeframe spanning MC and Up-to-Seven eras, competing-risks framework — are legitimate but modest and overlap substantially with prior European validation cohorts (van Hooff 2022, Pommergaard 2019). The proposed RETREAT+ modification adding tumor grade is explored but acknowledged as not improving predictive performance, limiting its contribution. Positioning in the introduction is adequate; direct comparators are acknowledged.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is generally readable with a clear IMRaD structure, and the abstract is quantitatively grounded with concrete recurrence and survival figures by risk category. However, there is a clearly truncated sentence in the Methods ('Patients were excluded from this study in case of' with no completion), the SPSS/R software citation contains a '[REDACTED]' artifact that should be fixed, and the Discussion is lengthy and repetitive, particularly restating RETREAT performance and the temporal-heterogeneity argument multiple times. Table/figure captions are referenced but somewhat terse, and the strengths/limitations framing in the Discussion rehearses results rather than concisely contextualizing them.

key_strengths: Appropriate use of competing-risks analysis for recurrence endpoint, acknowledging death as a competing event
Long follow-up (median 64 months, out to 15 years) spanning both Milan and Up-to-Seven eras in a 298-patient real-world European cohort
Confirms RETREAT discrimination across risk tiers with coherent HRs (medium 2.3, high 6.4) and clinically meaningful 5-year RFS separation (93% vs 78% vs 58%)
Clear clinical framing linking risk strata to surveillance and immunosuppression decisions
key_concerns: Truncated exclusion-criteria sentence in Section 2.1 leaves selection process unspecified; a software citation retains a '[REDACTED]' artifact
No discrimination (C-index/AUROC) or calibration metrics reported, which are core TRIPOD items for a prognostic model validation
No power calculation, no handling-of-missing-data description, and no era-stratified sensitivity analysis despite 22-year span
Novelty is incremental — multiple prior European/UK/UNOS validations exist, and the RETREAT+ extension did not improve prediction
No visible data-availability or code-sharing statement; reproducibility posture is minimal
Discussion is repetitive and over-long, rehashing results and strengths
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent but incremental single-center external validation of an established score with missing standard prognostic-model metrics (discrimination/calibration) and reporting gaps; fits a Tier 3 specialty oncology journal after major revisions to address TRIPOD items, complete the Methods, and tighten the Discussion.
